description: RECS is the U.S. Energy Information Administration's survey of a nationally representative sample of housing units, combining household reports of energy characteristics, usage patterns and demographics with data from energy suppliers to estimate costs and consumption for heating, cooling, appliances and other end uses. Interviewers traditionally collected the data; for 2020 EIA moved to web and mail forms. The 2024 survey collected responses from nearly 17,000 households in all 50 states and the District of Columbia and describes the estimated 132.5 million primary-residence homes. Recent releases: preliminary 2024 housing characteristics (March 2026), preliminary microdata with a user's guide (May 2026) and highlights (17 September 2026), with full 2024 data expected in spring 2027; monthly estimates for 2020 were published in May 2025. Access: tables, microdata and documentation from EIA; Catalyst Cooperative archives the raw inputs for 1993 to 2024 on Zenodo. Licence: U.S. government data in the public domain; free. Caveats: sample-based estimates, and end-use consumption is modelled. Simulation uses are residential stock energy models, appliance and occupant priors, and demand-response studies. Related records: CBECS, BuildOcc (which uses RECS priors) and the American Housing Survey.
